connection_authentication.note: Integrity in .ziv is provided by the AES-GCM tag (AEAD), not by an HMAC; the zivpn:// link has no MAC (AES-CBC + XML/JSON parse). PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 is a local key derivation, not connection authentication. No HMAC was traced to a connection-authentication purpose in the material reviewed (reference decoders + dossier). The connection_authentication field is NOT_OBSERVED per policy §2.2: that describes only the coverage reviewed, not a universal absence.
connection_authentication.rule: The mere presence of an HMAC library or a Mac.init call confirms nothing. No key values and no hook inputs/outputs are stored in this dossier.

limitations: No real .ziv file exported by app 2.2.5 (confirms the method and the export/import DES asymmetry end to end).
No real zivpn:// link observed; the scheme is from legacy text handlers, not from the app manifest (the 2026-11-14 dossier found no own URI scheme in the APK).

The offline APK itself was NOT built in this VM (no Android SDK/NDK/Gradle toolchain here); the production C++ was verified on the host against Mbed TLS 3.6.7 and 2.28.8, and the Gradle build is covered by the offline-native-apk CI workflow. No emulator/device test was run.

The legacy Kotlin ZivPort (src/main/java, non-distributed baseline) still lacks the DES inner layer: it opens export-style .ziv only and fails legacy (DES-layered) files. It is NOT compiled into the offline APK; the native decoder is the offline implementation. Fixing it is a separate follow-up.
The offline app's visible supported-text label still lists only NPV Tunnel, NetMod Syna and Dark Tunnel (OfflineText.kt, untouched: no UI/design changes in this task).
